newsitem.title: USA: Family in assisted suicide sues deceased's husband. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Family in assisted suicide sues deceased's husband. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]

text.p: Family members of an ailing woman whose husband helped her commit suicide said on Wednesday they had filed a $10 million wrongful death lawsuit against him.

The family was also seeking to prevent George DeLury from profiting from a book he wrote, "But What If She Wants to Die?" in which he admits suffocating his wife Myrna Lebov, 52, with plastic bags after giving her a lethal drug overdose.
Lebov, who was suffering from multiple sclerosis, died on July 4, 1995. Her husband pleaded guilty to a reduced charge of attempted manslaughter and spent four months in jail.
Lebov's family claims she did not intend to commit suicide and was coerced by DeLury, who considered her a burden.
"She told us she did not want to die," Lebov's sister Beverly Sloane said. "She was a victim of psychological coercion and murder."
The lawsuit seeking $10 million (corrects from $10,000) in punitive damages was filed on Wednesday in State Supreme Court in Manhattan, the family's attorney Steven Mintz said.

The lawsuit also cites a New York state law that prevents convicted criminals from profiting from their crimes. DeLury has said he would donate proceeds from the book to the Hemlock Society, which aids people in committing suicide.
Double jeopardy rules protect him against further criminal charges in the case.
